INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
DEUTSCHE BANK
Anshika Sharma, B.Tech Computers (2020 - 24)
Deutsche Bank visited our campus in August 2023 to hire final year students for the
role of Graduate Technical Analyst.
Criteria:
1. CPI: 7 and above
2. Branches : Computers, IT & EXTC(Electronics and Telecommunication)
Rounds:
1. Online Coding Test.
2. Offline Technical Round-1.
3. Offline Technical Round-2.
4. Offline Professional-fitment Round.
5. Offline HR Round.
Round 1 - Online coding round (90 mins)
It was an online test on HackerEarth platform. There were 3 coding questions in this
round. The questions were of easy-medium difficulty. The scores for questions were
20,50,50 respectively.
1. Given 2 resources with powers A and B respectively. At each second, you have to select
one resource out of 2 to run the software.
The power of the resource at the time of selection should be greater than 1. Every second,
the power of the selected resource gets reduced by 2 and the power of unselected
resource gets charged by 1.
The software stops when at least one resource has 0 power.
You are given integers A and B. Print the maximum number of seconds your software
can run if you select the resources optimally.

2. Given a dictionary consisting of N words and a query word S. You need to auto suggest
the best word from the dictionary that is closest to S.
Two words are first compared by their Levenshtein distance to the word S. If two words
have the same Levenshtein distance, then the lexicographically smaller word is given
priority.
Notes
Levenshtein distance between two strings is defined as the minimum number of edits
required to obtain one string from the other. An "edit" is defined by either an insertion of
a character, a deletion of a character, or a replacement of a character.
All the words and the query word S consist of lowercase alphabets only.
Function description
Complete the function solve. This function takes the following 3 parameters and returns
the required answer:
N: Represents the number of words in the dictionary
words: Represents the dictionary
S: Represents the query word
3. Backlinks are links from other websites to a particular web resource, and they play a
crucial role in the SEO of pages.
You are given N web page titles and corresponding arrays that contain the number of
backlinks for each web page. The objective is to rank the web pages in descending order
based on the number of backlinks they have.
Note: If two or more web pages have the same number of backlinks, maintain their
original order.
Function description
Complete the function Sorter. This function takes 2 parameters as arguments and returns
the strings:
WebPage: Represents an array of strings that contains the webpage titles
Backlinks: Represents an array of integers that contains the backlink count
40 people were shortlisted for the interviews.
2

Round 2 - Technical Interview round 1 (~45-50 mins)
Offline interviews were scheduled on 9th August, 2023 starting from 9:00 AM. They asked
questions on a lot of things including my resume. internship, Projects, DSA, OOPS, OS and
DBMS.
●
The interviewer gave a brief introduction before the conversation began. Following that, I
had the opportunity to introduce myself.
●
She then looked over my resume, asked about my projects.
●
The subjects I have studied. I replied with DSA, OOPS, DBMS and OS. Asked questions
from almost all of them. I don't remember all of them. But some of them were: What is
oops. Detailed explanation of four pillars of oops. I explained in detail with real life
examples. Then asked about Functional Programming Paradigm, difference between
encapsulation and abstraction, Exception handling.
●
Then she asked me to write a basic sql query.
●
Some questions on react like react hooks, asynchronous functions, etc were asked. Then
some questions on HTML, CSS and javascript like different data types present in js,
Difference between “ == “ and “ === “ operators, How to include CSS in the webpage,
What is the difference between inline, inline-block, and block, why <! DOCTYPE html>
tag is used in any html file.
●
Moving to DSA, she asked how to reverse a linked list, how to swap 2 variables without
using a third variable, removing duplicates from a string.
●
Some questions on OS were asked like what are Scheduling Algorithms, different types
of scheduling algorithms.
●
You have a birthday cake and have to cut it into 8 equal pieces by making 3 cuts only.
How do you do it?
And in this way, the interview almost came to an end. At last, she asked if I had some questions.
3

Round 3 - Technical Interview round 2 (~45-50 mins)
●
Introduce yourself.
●
Again touched Internship, DSA, OOPS, OS, Projects.
●
Intersection of two linked lists.
●
Height of binary tree.
●
Find the maximum and minimum node in a Binary Search Tree.
●
Finding the sum of digits of a number until the sum becomes a single digit.
●
Four pillars of OOPS
●
Thrashing in OS
●
Difference between arrays and linked lists.
●
Static and dynamic allocation.
●
Method overriding, operator overloading.
●
What is data structure and types of data structures?
●
Then moved to the tech stack I used in my projects. Asked various questions like what is
npm, what is express, what is middleware, basic flow of any node.js file, etc.
Round 4 - Professional Fitness Round (~25-30 mins)
●
Introduce yourself.
●
How was your day till now? Are you tired?
●
Asked about my internship experience in detail and The project I have worked on. Did
some cross-questioning.
●
Then about my projects, what was the problem statement, tech stack, architecture
diagram etc.
●
You have a perfectly cylindrical glass filled with water. Without any kind of measuring
device, how can you empty the glass so it is exactly half full?
●
Why DB?
4

Round 5 - HR Round (~20-30 mins)
●
Introduce yourself.
●
Asked about my internship and projects.
●
Given that I had taken on a leadership role within one of the committees, I was asked
about the team size. Additionally, I was asked to elaborate on my strategies to ensure
inclusive participation among team members. Furthermore, I was asked to outline my
approach in the event that certain team members were not fully engaged or invested in
the task at hand.
●
What would I prefer, frontend or backend?
●
Any questions I had.
Tips:
●
Ensure you have a strong grasp of the fundamentals – these are the building blocks that
will naturally come together as you proceed
●
Stay composed and remember that things will align as you go along. Approach the
process with a relaxed mindset and give it your best shot.
●
Confidence is key. Remember, no one is expected to possess all-encompassing
knowledge. Your attitude is crucial – show a genuine willingness to learn and improve.
●
While knowledge is important, the ability to effectively communicate and share your
understanding holds equal weight. Express yourself clearly and articulate your thoughts.
The focus is on your problem-solving approach and your thinking process.
●
Don't underestimate the impact of a positive attitude. Maintain your composure and
ensure that nervousness or anxiety doesn't hinder your performance. Techniques like
taking deep breaths or engaging in activities that soothe you can be valuable.
●
When discussing your projects, thorough preparation is crucial.
All the best!! You can do it!! :)
If you have any queries, feel free to drop an email at anshikash03@gmail.com
